notes: Confirms the model-dependence hypothesis: +25pt delta on Sonnet 5 vs +17pt on Fable 5 (iteration-1). With-skill is saturated at 100% under both models; the delta grew because the BASELINE degraded under the weaker model — eval-0 baseline fell 5/10 (Fable) -> 4/10 (Sonnet) with the same 'prose instead of mechanism' failure signature, plus new regressions on problem-brief completeness and sync-email sanctioning that Fable's baseline passed unaided.

EVAL-1 DECONTAMINATION (this update): eval-1's runs were re-executed under the new isolation protocol (evals/RUN-PROTOCOL.md). First isolated attempt STILL got contaminated — the baseline agent followed the fixture's 'GENERATED by rebuild-kit render_guide.py' breadcrumb and located the skill by absolute path despite running in /private/tmp (archived under _contaminated/). The clean rerun required physically removing the skill implementation from the machine for the duration of the baseline run.

The clean eval-1 result is a genuine 8/8 vs 8/8 tie, now PROVEN uncontaminated: the grader re-ran the real renderer against the baseline's output and found visible divergence (paraphrased manifest strings, flat bullet format vs the renderer's structured template) — exactly what honest hand-editing looks like, where contamination had produced byte-identical output. The tie is real and is the architecture's intended property: the workspace itself steers any competent session through a correct spec-patch. What the skill still adds on this eval: protocol compliance (guide genuinely re-rendered vs hand-forked — the clean baseline's decisions.md now DRIFTS from what the renderer would emit, the exact two-sources-of-truth failure the never-hand-edit rule exists to prevent) and a P9-lite re-audit that caught a real latent bug (legacy computes slugify(title) twice — insert vs response — which becomes a stored-vs-returned slug mismatch once slug generation is stateful/uniqueness-aware). No current assertion scores either; both are proposed tightenings.

Contamination lesson for anyone reusing this eval harness: self-describing fixtures actively recruit agents into finding their referenced toolchain — sibling-directory separation is NOT sufficient isolation; /private/tmp isolation is NOT sufficient either. Only physical absence of the skill (or a container) produced a clean no-skill arm.

Interesting secondary finding preserved from the contaminated attempt: even having read the skill's renderer source, that baseline still violated the skill's contract-freeze convention (added a UNIQUE constraint to the frozen legacy DDL) — while the clean baseline independently REASONED its way to leaving ddl.sql alone. Convention-compliance is not reliably absorbed by reading one script; it comes from the playbooks.

Cost: with-skill averages ~258k tokens / ~30min vs baseline ~104k / ~9.5min under Sonnet. Sonnet's baseline is costlier than Fable's (~104k vs ~33k) while scoring worse — the weaker model isn't cheaper without structure, just less effective per token.

Two real skill bugs found and fixed in scripts/scaffold.py this round: (1) the pre-commit guard rejected the scaffolder's own initial commit (fixed: exempt the pre-HEAD commit); (2) pin_legacy() could silently pin legacy_ref to an ANCESTOR repo's SHA when legacy/ has no .git (fixed: require git rev-parse --show-toplevel to resolve to legacy/ itself). Both are 'evidence or it doesn't ship' correctness failures the skill exists to prevent — regression-test before shipping v1.

n=1 per configuration per model — treat deltas as directional. The eval-0 mechanism-vs-prose signal is consistent across both models and mechanistically explained, which carries more weight than the raw numbers.
